narration: Sometimes one coding agent handles the whole task. Sometimes a main agent delegates parts of the work to other agents.
voiceDirection: Clear and neutral. Do not imply more agents are always better.

narration: The main agent is the orchestrator. It keeps the overall goal, decides what can be split, and tracks how the pieces fit together.
It can delegate research, frontend work, backend changes, and testing as separate subtasks, each with a smaller context.
voiceDirection: Give each subtask a clean beat.

narration: Those subtasks can run in parallel when they are independent. That can reduce waiting and keep each agent focused on less context.
onScreenText: Independent work can run in parallel.

narration: But parallel work creates a coordination problem. Two agents can make assumptions that conflict, touch the same file, or solve different versions of the task.
That is why outputs should return to an integration step. The orchestrator compares results, resolves conflicts, and keeps the final implementation consistent.
captionText: Integration is part of the job.

narration: Some tasks are still better with one agent, especially when the work is tightly connected or small enough to fit in one clear context.
onScreenText: Not every task needs multiple agents.
captionText: Split only when the work actually separates.

narration: The useful question is not one agent or many. It is whether the task can be divided cleanly, coordinated well, and reviewed as one result.
